LESSON: ENTREPRENEURIAL OPPORTUNITIES IN SOCIAL STUDIES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Personal development
Topic 1.2: Entrepreneurial Opportunities in Social Studies

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Entrepreneurial Opportunities in Social Studies. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is entrepreneurship 2. Which entrepreneurial opportunities exist in society?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality
2. describe requirements for social entrepreneurial opportunities in the world of work
3. appreciate entrepreneurial opportunities in social studies

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ENTREPRENEURIAL OPPORTUNITIES IN SOCIAL STUDIES
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Entrepreneurial Opportunities in Social Studies helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: ENTREPRENEURIAL OPPORTUNITIES IN SOCIAL STUDIES
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Identify entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality

What this means
In this part you learn to identify entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Entrepreneurial Opportunities in Social Studies” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe requirements for social entrepreneurial opportunities in the world of work

What this means
In this part you learn to describe requirements for social entrepreneurial opportunities in the world of work. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe requirements for social entrepreneurial opportunities in the world of work.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Entrepreneurial Opportunities in Social Studies.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe requirements for social entrepreneurial opportunities in the world of work. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate entrepreneurial opportunities in social studies

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate entrepreneurial opportunities in social studies. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate entrepreneurial opportunities in social studies.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate entrepreneurial opportunities in social studies. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Entrepreneurial Opportunities in Social Studies is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Entrepreneurial Opportunities in Social Studies” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: identify entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Entrepreneurial Opportunities in Social Studies. (skill: describe requirements for social entrepreneurial opportunities in the world of work)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: appreciate entrepreneurial opportunities in social studies)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Entrepreneurial Opportunities in Social Studies to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality.
3. Practise this skill: describe requirements for social entrepreneurial opportunities in the world of work.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate entrepreneurial opportunities in social studies.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Entrepreneurial Opportunities in Social Studies from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Entrepreneurial Opportunities in Social Studies: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Entrepreneurial Opportunities in Social Studies?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is entrepreneurship 2. Which entrepreneurial opportunities exist in society?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Entrepreneurial Opportunities in Social Studies means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality.
5. Be able to: describe requirements for social entrepreneurial opportunities in the world of work.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
